ai.description: The Agror Agama reaches 12 cm in snout-vent length. It is grey-brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark dorsal blotches. Distinctive features include a flattened body and granular scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: To distinguish *Laudakia agrorensis*, look for the distinct, enlarged, spinose scales on the sides of the neck and flanks, which are absent in similar Indian agamas.
ai.habitat: *Laudakia agrorensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and cliffs in the Himalayan foothills, typically at altitudes between 600 and 2,000 meters within scrubland environments.
ai.behavior: The Agror agama is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on rocky outcrops to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for insects and plant matter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laudakia agrorensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally between May and July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Laudakia agrorensis* is found in the western Himalayas, specifically across northern Pakistan and the Indian states of Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh.
